newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady on Wednesday in moderate trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. May factory orders data and the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, dealers said.
Factory orders for May are forecast to show a decline of 0.2 percent compared with a 1.2 percent increase reported in April.

"The market was steady to a little bit easier in the morning on some position adjustments. All eyes are on the outcome of the FOMC meeting, but it is expected to leave monetary policy unchanged," a local dealer said.

"Some people are also waiting for tonight's release of the factory orders figures for more clues to market direction, but unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I dont' think there will be much impact," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Wednesday/Thursday was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent. Thursday/Friday and week-fixed were unchanged from Tuesday's common 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16, nine-months eased 1/16 point to 6 5-7/8 and twelve- months unchanged at 6-1/8 6 percent. - P. Theseira (65-870-3085)
